chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from someone he mentioned, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from his father who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you hear knowledge, apply it, and let your hearts be expansive. For when knowledge becomes abundant in the heart of a man who cannot bear it, Satan gains power over him. So when Satan disputes with you, confront him with what you know; for the plot of Satan has always been weak.'
So I said: 'And what is it that we should know?' He said: 'Dispute with him using whatever of the power of God, Mighty and Majestic, has become manifest to you.'

key_terms.العلم: Knowledge — here understood as applied, embodied religious learning, not mere information
key_terms.فَاسْتَعْمِلُوهُ: Utilize/apply it — active imperative demanding the actualization of knowledge in conduct
key_terms.قدرة الله: The Power of God — observable signs of divine omnipotence in creation used to counter satanic doubt
key_terms.كيد الشيطان: The plot/scheme of Satan — Quran 4:76 affirms this is inherently weak

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about applying knowledge and resisting Satan?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) commands believers to actively apply religious knowledge — not merely accumulate it — and to keep their hearts open and expansive. He warns that a heart too narrow to contain knowledge becomes vulnerable to satanic influence, and gives practical guidance: resist Satan not through abstract argument but by citing the manifest signs of God's omnipotence one witnesses in creation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muihammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Layli, from his father who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whenever you hear the knowledge, so utilize it and let your hearts be accommodating, for the knowledge, when it is abundant in the heart of a man, would not tolerate the Satan<sup>la</sup> to have power over him. So when the Satan<sup>la</sup> disputes with you, so pile upon him<sup>la</sup> with what you are recognising, for the plots of the Satan<sup>la</sup> would always be weak’.

So I said, ‘And what is that which we should be recognising?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Be at odds with him with whatever appears to you from the Power of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from the one mentioned from Muhammad ibn ’Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Layla from his father who has said the following.

“Imam abu Ja‘far (a.s.) has said, ‘When you hear knowledge you must utilize it and your hearts must become more open. When knowledge increases in one’s heart it becomes harder to bear and Satan may over power him. If Satan would dispute with you move on him with whatever you know. The plots of Satan are weak.”
I asked the Imam (a.s.) “What is it that we know?’” The Imam replied, “Fight him with whatever of the power of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, has come to light before you.”
